Title: Diagnosis
Details: The corresponding issue report describes that tooltip text in the UI is displayed with HTML entities such as " instead of the intended characters. This strongly suggests a missing escaping or decoding step in tooltip generation. Inspecting the implementation of StandardToolTipTagFragmentGenerator.generateToolTipFragment reveals that it directly returns the toolTipText without applying any escaping. Recent issue reports mention similar encoding or escaping problems in related UI components, reinforcing the suspicion that this method lacks proper handling. The behavior observed in the code matches the issue report's symptoms, indicating that missing escaping in this method is the likely root cause.

After providing this diagnosis, you will be prompted to suggest which methods would be the best locations to be fixed. The answers should be in the form of `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` without commentary (one per line), as your answer will be automatically processed before finally being presented to the user.

messages.content:
Title: Diagnosis
Details:
- What the failing test does:
  - testReadWinZipArchive opens a WinZip-created archive with useUnicodeExtraFields=true and then asserts it can read three entries by name via ZipFile.getEntry(name) followed by ZipFile.getInputStream(entry).

- Where the failure manifests:
  - ZipFile.getInputStream(ZipArchiveEntry) looks up the entry’s data via entries.get(ze). If the lookup returns null, getInputStream returns null.
  - The report matches this: getInputStream returns null for ZipArchiveEntry objects previously obtained from getEntry/getEntries.

- How entries are built:
  - In ZipFile’s constructor, populateFromCentralDirectory() reads the central directory and creates a ZipArchiveEntry per file. Each entry is inserted into:
    - entries: a LinkedHashMap<ZipArchiveEntry, OffsetEntry>
    - nameMap: a Map<String, ZipArchiveEntry> mapping names to the same ZipArchiveEntry instance
  - For entries without the UTF-8 flag and with useUnicodeExtraFields=true, readCentralDirectoryEntry stores the raw filename/comment bytes into a noUTF8Flag map keyed by the ZipArchiveEntry.

- What happens next for WinZip archives with Unicode extra fields:
  - resolveLocalFileHeaderData iterates over the entries map’s keys (ZipArchiveEntry instances) and:
    - Reads the local file header extra data and calls ze.setExtra(localExtraData)
    - If the entry was recorded in noUTF8Flag, calls ZipUtil.setNameAndCommentFromExtraFields to update the entry’s name/comment from the Unicode extra fields; if the name changes, nameMap is updated to point from the new name to the same ZipArchiveEntry instance.

- The core defect: mutating map keys after insertion
  - The entries map uses ZipArchiveEntry objects as keys. resolveLocalFileHeaderData mutates those objects by:
    - ze.setExtra(localExtraData), which changes the “local extra” data associated with the entry.
    - Potentially updating the name/comment via setNameAndCommentFromExtraFields.
  - ZipArchiveEntry’s equality (and by contract its hashCode) depends on many mutable fields (including name, comment, time, method, sizes, CRC, and the extra data arrays). The code itself comments that changing the name changes the hash code.
  - Because the keys’ hash-relevant state changes after they were put into the LinkedHashMap, the map’s internal bucketing no longer matches the key’s current hashCode. This breaks lookups, even if you pass the same ZipArchiveEntry instance:
    - getInputStream calls entries.get(ze)
    - HashMap uses ze’s current hashCode to locate a bucket, but the entry was stored under its old hashCode in a different bucket, so the lookup fails and returns null.

- Secondary symptom:
  - resolveLocalFileHeaderData also looks up the entry in entriesWithoutUTF8Flag via containsKey(ze) after calling setExtra(localExtraData). If hashCode changes due to the extra data, this lookup may fail too, and the Unicode name/comment won’t be applied. Regardless, the mutation already broke the entries map.

- Why this impacts the test:
  - testReadWinZipArchive uses Unicode extra fields (WinZip style) by constructing ZipFile with useUnicodeExtraFields=true.
  - After construction, getEntry(name) retrieves the ZipArchiveEntry from nameMap (updated if the name changed).
  - Passing that ZipArchiveEntry to getInputStream leads to entries.get(ze) returning null due to the mutated key, so getInputStream returns null, causing the test to fail.

- Root cause summary:
  - ZipArchiveEntry instances are used as keys in a HashMap and then mutated (extra fields and possibly name/comment) during resolveLocalFileHeaderData. This changes their hashCode and breaks the entries map, making getInputStream unable to find the corresponding OffsetEntry for valid entries. The code even contains a comment acknowledging that changing the name changes the hash code and that the map needs to be reconstructed, but it isn’t rebuilt.

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
